instruction: The text size is too small for me to read comfortably. Could you increase the font scaling to at least 1.5 times the normal size?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: TEXT_SCALE=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface text-scaling-factor 2>/dev/null | grep -oE "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+" | head -1); if [ -n "$TEXT_SCALE" ] && [ "$(echo "$TEXT_SCALE >= 1.5" | bc -l 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" = "1" ]; then echo "Large text scaling enabled (factor: $TEXT_SCALE)"; else echo "Text scaling below threshold"; fi

metadata.explanation: Similar to original but requires text-scaling-factor >= 1.5 (higher threshold). Task requires enabling large text and adjusting to 1.5x via Settings > Accessibility. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric with vm_command_line getter.

llm_judge_reasons: Correct state extraction: Command properly reads GNOME text-scaling-factor via gsettings, which is the correct system setting for text size
Correct threshold verification: Command checks if scaling factor >= 1.5 using bc comparison, matching the instruction requirement 'at least 1.5 times'
Complete coverage: Evaluator verifies the exact requirement from the instruction (text scaling >= 1.5)
Robust implementation: Command includes timeout, error handling (2>/dev/null), fallback logic (|| echo 0), and proper numeric comparison
Correct expected values: Success message 'Large text scaling enabled' and failure message 'Text scaling below threshold' correctly distinguish between passing and failing states
No postconfig needed: System settings persist and can be read at any time without special setup
